project_scope.selection_mode: modern broad family with local Yucca visual anchor
project_scope.note: Modern broad family: the current Master Plant Pool contains eight genera; the installed canonical species are Yucca anchors only. Yucca rosettes are not a universal Asparagaceae family trait.

family_diagnostics.where_to_look_first: LOOK HERE FIRST: sort eight Master Pool genera into (1) rosettes Yucca/Agave/Hesperaloe/Manfreda, (2) grasslike tufts Nolina/Dasylirion, or (3) spring bulbs Camassia/Androstephium. Then check leaf edge, tepal/stamen architecture, ovary position and fruit. Yucca rosettes are NOT universal to Asparagaceae.
family_diagnostics.broad_family: Modern Asparagaceae is morphologically broad; reproductive characters commonly include 6 tepals, 6 stamens and a 3-locular ovary, but ovary position and fruit type vary.
family_diagnostics.local_yucca: Stiff fibrous leaves in rosettes or on trunks; large terminal flower panicles; 6 fleshy tepals; 6 stamens; 3-carpellate fruit.
family_diagnostics.field_tip: Yucca has true leaves and no cactus areoles. Use leaf texture/armature plus flower/fruit for species.
family_diagnostics.yucca_anchor_look_here_first: For local Yucca, start with rosette/trunk architecture and the true fibrous leaves. Inspect terminal spine/margin fibers, then the terminal panicle with 3+3 tepals and the fruit.

family_diagnostics.shared_morphology_and_exceptions: Modern Asparagaceae includes rosettes, grasslike tufts and spring bulbs in the local pool. Flowers commonly have 3+3 tepals and six stamens, but ovary position, leaf armature, fruit type and floral form vary. Do not generalize Yucca spines, white pendent flowers, or yucca-moth pollination to the family.

visual_lesson.teaching_order: whole plant → diagnostic structure → reproductive confirmation → tie-breaker
visual_lesson.intro: The local lesson is really 'how to read Yucca' while remembering that Yucca is only one form inside broad Asparagaceae.

steps.title: 1 · Read the rosette
steps.look_for: Basal/terminal cluster of true fibrous leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Separates Yucca from superficially spiny cacti and begins the species comparison.

steps.title: 2 · Inspect the leaf
steps.look_for: Leaf stiffness, twist, color, marginal threads and terminal spine.
steps.why_it_matters: Vegetative Yucca ID often starts here.

steps.title: 3 · Compare a narrow-leaved species
steps.look_for: Narrower flexible leaves and different margin/fiber pattern.
steps.why_it_matters: Builds a useful local Yucca contrast before flowering.

steps.title: 4 · Add trunked architecture
steps.look_for: Arborescent/trunked habit with stout rosettes and strongly armed leaves.
steps.why_it_matters: Shows how much vegetative architecture varies within local Yucca.

steps.title: 5 · Confirm the flower/fruit
steps.look_for: Large terminal panicle, six tepals and 3-carpellate fruit.
steps.why_it_matters: Reproductive characters confirm the local genus/family placement.

steps.title: 6 · Route the eight genera by plant architecture
steps.photo_role: matched rosette / grasslike tuft / bulb triptych
steps.look_for: Separate Yucca/Agave/Hesperaloe/Manfreda from Nolina/Dasylirion and Camassia/Androstephium before naming a genus.
steps.why_it_matters: Yucca anchors alone do not cover the family.

steps.title: 7 · Compare superior and inferior ovaries
steps.photo_role: matched longitudinal Yucca and Agave flower sections
steps.look_for: Locate the seed-bearing chamber relative to tepal and stamen attachment. Yucca/Hesperaloe superior, Agave/Manfreda inferior in the FNA agave-lineage key.
steps.why_it_matters: Leaf similarity can conceal major reproductive differences.

steps.title: 8 · Read tiny flowers and spring bulbs
steps.photo_role: Nolina/Dasylirion fruit sections and Camassia/Androstephium flower centers
steps.look_for: Nolina three-locular versus Dasylirion one-locular fruit; Camassia free stamens versus Androstephium staminal crown.
steps.why_it_matters: These four genera are easily missed by a Yucca-only lesson.

comparisons.title: Yucca vs Cactaceae
comparisons.rule: Yucca has true fibrous leaves in a rosette and lacks areoles. Cacti have specialized areoles and highly modified/reduced leaves.

comparisons.title: Asparagaceae vs Iridaceae
comparisons.rule: Both can have six showy tepals, but local Iridaceae commonly have three stamens while Camassia and other Asparagaceae examples commonly have six. Verify an open flower.

comparisons.title: Asparagaceae vs Amaryllidaceae
comparisons.rule: Spathe-bracted umbels and inferior ovaries often suggest amaryllids, but Allium has a superior ovary; combine characters rather than relying on one.

comparisons.title: Nolina/Dasylirion vs Poaceae/Cyperaceae
comparisons.rule: These grasslike Asparagaceae have tiny tepaled flowers and capsules, not grass spikelets or sedge achenes; check a fertile stem.

visual_lesson.caveat: Do not generalize Yucca's rosette/spines to all modern Asparagaceae. This is a local eight-genus routing guide, not a universal family key. FNA Agavoideae characters should not be imposed on all Asparagaceae.
